outcome: birth parameters (gestational week, body weight, body length, head, and chest circumferences)
cohort: The study included 74 pregnant women with a mean age of 31.9 years, BMI of 23.6 kg/m2, and an average gestational duration of 38.5 weeks.
finding: Environmental tobacco smoke exposure was associated with a decrease in birth length by at least 1 cm and potentially served as an independent risk factor for fetal growth restriction, although neither PM2.5/PM10 nor ETS was linked to low birth weight or small for gestational age.
